<issue>
InlineShape height setter incorrectly modifies width property

#### Description

When setting the height of an InlineShape, the width property gets modified instead of the height. This causes incorrect dimensions to be applied to inline shapes in Word documents.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches

# Create a document and add an image
doc = Document()
paragraph = doc.paragraphs[0]
run = paragraph.runs[0] if paragraph.runs else paragraph.add_run()

# Add an inline shape (image)
inline_shape = run.add_picture('image.png', width=Inches(2), height=Inches(1))

# Try to change the height
original_width = inline_shape.width
inline_shape.height = Inches(3)

# The width should remain unchanged, but it gets modified instead
print(f"Original width: {original_width}")
print(f"Current width: {inline_shape.width}")  # This will be different
print(f"Current height: {inline_shape.height}")  # This may not be what was set
```

Also affects shape type detection - pictures are incorrectly identified as charts and vice versa, and smart art detection returns wrong values.
</issue>
